nodes.title: What a Linux system actually is
outcomes: Distinguish hardware, firmware, kernel, userspace, distribution, shell, terminal, and application.
Trace a simple command from user intent to userspace program to kernel-mediated effects.

nodes.title: Build a safe Linux learning laboratory
outcomes: Choose between host, VM, container, namespace, and disk-image experiments.
Recognize which commands can alter or destroy system state and how to make experiments reversible.

nodes.title: The command line as a language interface
outcomes: Identify prompt, command, arguments, options, operands, exit status, stdout, and stderr.
Run and inspect commands without treating command strings as magic incantations.

nodes.title: Learn to ask Linux for help
outcomes: Use man sections, --help, help, info, and official documentation deliberately.
Identify whether a question concerns a shell builtin, utility, syscall, file format, or administrator command.

nodes.title: Paths, names, and the single filesystem tree
outcomes: Reason about absolute/relative paths, root, current directory, parent directory, hidden names, and path resolution.

nodes.title: Navigate and inspect directories
outcomes: Use pwd, cd, ls and related inspection tools while predicting path effects before running them.

nodes.title: Create, copy, move, and remove files safely
outcomes: Manipulate files/directories and distinguish replacement, recursive behavior, and destructive operations.

nodes.title: Read and edit text without losing context
outcomes: Inspect text with cat/less/head/tail and edit configuration or source text with a terminal editor.
Choose tools based on file size and task rather than habit.

nodes.title: Quoting, globbing, and expansion
outcomes: Predict when the shell transforms text before a program receives arguments.
Use quotes, wildcards, variables, and command substitution without accidental expansion.

nodes.title: Standard streams, redirection, and pipelines
outcomes: Connect programs with stdin/stdout/stderr and explain which process opens each redirected file.
Build simple pipelines and inspect their failure modes.

nodes.title: Search, filter, count, sort, and transform text
outcomes: Compose grep, sort, uniq, cut, tr, wc, head, and tail into transparent data-processing pipelines.

nodes.title: Identity, ownership, and permission intuition
outcomes: Explain user/group identity, file ownership, rwx permissions, and why privileged operations differ.

nodes.title: Processes, jobs, and signals: first mental model
outcomes: Distinguish program from process, PID from command name, foreground from background, and graceful termination from forced termination.

nodes.title: Software packages, repositories, and updates
outcomes: Explain why distributions package software, how repositories and metadata fit together, and how updates change system state.

nodes.title: Networks from a Linux user’s point of view
outcomes: Distinguish local host, interface, address, route, DNS name, port, client/server, and remote shell.
Perform a minimal evidence-based connectivity check.

nodes.title: Tour the living system: /etc, /var, /proc, /sys, /dev
outcomes: Explain the different roles of persistent configuration, mutable state/logs, process/kernel views, device model, and device nodes.

nodes.title: Shell environment, PATH, startup files, and exit status
outcomes: Trace variable/export/PATH behavior from shell startup to command execution.
Use exit status as data rather than merely noticing error text.

nodes.title: Find files and build safe command selections
outcomes: Use find predicates/actions and xargs safely, including whitespace/NUL-delimited cases.

nodes.title: Regular expressions and stream transformation
outcomes: Use basic/extended regular expressions deliberately and apply grep/sed/awk to structured text problems.

nodes.title: Archives, compression, checksums, and integrity
outcomes: Distinguish archiving from compression and use checksums to verify content transfer/integrity.

nodes.title: Metadata, inodes, hard links, and symbolic links
outcomes: Separate filenames, directory entries, inode-like metadata, hard-link identity, and symbolic-link path references.

nodes.title: Permissions beyond rwx: umask, special bits, and ACLs
outcomes: Predict effective access under owner/group/other, umask, set-ID/sticky semantics, and ACL extensions.

nodes.title: Users, groups, sudo, and account lifecycle
outcomes: Create and reason about accounts/groups, password/shadow state, privilege delegation, and least-privilege sudo policy.

nodes.title: Process trees, sessions, jobs, signals, and resource views
outcomes: Inspect parent/child relationships, sessions/process groups, job control, signals, and basic resource consumption.

nodes.title: systemd services and units without memorizing systemctl
outcomes: Explain unit state, service supervision, enablement versus activation, and common systemctl operations from the unit model.

nodes.title: Logs as evidence: journald and traditional log files
outcomes: Query and correlate journal events, boot boundaries, service logs, kernel messages, and persistent log files.

nodes.title: Time, clocks, time zones, synchronization, and scheduled work
outcomes: Distinguish wall clock/monotonic time/RTC, understand time zones/NTP, and choose cron versus systemd timers for scheduled work.

nodes.title: Storage devices, partitions, filesystems, mounts, and swap
outcomes: Trace a path from block device through partition/filesystem/mount point and distinguish persistent mount configuration from runtime state.

nodes.title: Addresses, routes, DNS, ports, and sockets
outcomes: Read interface/address/route/socket state with modern tools and use the evidence to localize connectivity failures.

nodes.title: SSH trust, keys, host identity, and secure transfer
outcomes: Explain user authentication versus host authentication and use key-based remote access and file transfer safely.

nodes.title: Distribution families, repositories, package formats, and portability boundaries
outcomes: Separate Linux/POSIX semantics from distribution policy and compare package/service/configuration differences without duplicating whole lessons per distro.

nodes.title: From power-on to userspace: the boot story
outcomes: Explain firmware, bootloader, kernel, initramfs, root filesystem, PID 1, and userspace activation as one causal chain.

nodes.title: Devices, device nodes, sysfs, and udev
outcomes: Relate hardware discovery, kernel devices, sysfs, uevents, /dev nodes, and userspace device management.

nodes.title: Shell scripting foundations
outcomes: Write small Bash programs with variables, conditions, loops, functions, input validation, and meaningful exit statuses.

nodes.title: A disciplined Linux troubleshooting method
outcomes: Form hypotheses, collect minimally invasive evidence, isolate layers, reproduce failures, and avoid random command trial-and-error.

nodes.title: Robust shell programs: errors, traps, arrays, and interfaces
outcomes: Design shell programs that handle errors/cleanup, preserve argument boundaries, expose useful interfaces, and avoid common set -e/word-splitting traps.

nodes.title: File descriptors and the system-call boundary
outcomes: Connect shell redirection to process file-descriptor tables and introduce open/read/write/close/dup as kernel interfaces.

nodes.title: fork, exec, wait, environment, and descriptor inheritance
outcomes: Explain Unix process creation/overlay and predict what state is inherited or replaced across fork/exec.

nodes.title: Signals in detail: delivery, masks, handlers, and races
outcomes: Reason about asynchronous signal delivery, masks, handlers, default actions, and race-prone patterns.

nodes.title: IPC: pipes, FIFOs, Unix sockets, shared memory, and queues
outcomes: Choose IPC mechanisms based on lifetime, addressing, buffering, synchronization, and data-sharing requirements.

nodes.title: /proc as a process and kernel observability interface
outcomes: Interpret process/kernel state in procfs while distinguishing snapshots, counters, tunables, and per-process namespaces.

nodes.title: Virtual memory from userspace: mappings, faults, and residency
outcomes: Explain address spaces, mmap, page faults, anonymous/file-backed memory, copy-on-write, and why RSS/VSZ are imperfect summaries.

nodes.title: VFS, inodes, dentries, page cache, and open files
outcomes: Relate path lookup, VFS objects, open-file state, page cache, and filesystem implementations.

nodes.title: The Linux storage stack: block devices, device mapper, LVM, RAID, encryption
outcomes: Trace I/O through block-device layers and design safe partition/LVM/RAID/dm-crypt layouts in disposable labs.

nodes.title: Filesystem consistency, journaling, snapshots, and recovery
outcomes: Explain crash-consistency goals, journaling/checking, snapshots, and recovery tradeoffs without treating fsck as a universal repair command.

nodes.title: Boot internals: UEFI, bootloaders, initramfs, kernel command line, and rescue
outcomes: Diagnose boot stages and modify boot/initramfs/kernel-command-line behavior safely in a recoverable environment.

nodes.title: systemd dependency graphs and activation mechanisms
outcomes: Reason about ordering versus requirement dependencies, targets, templates, environment, socket/path/timer activation, and failure propagation.

nodes.title: Kernel device events and udev rules
outcomes: Trace device events from kernel to userspace and write/test narrowly scoped udev rules without unstable device-name assumptions.

nodes.title: Linux networking in practice: routing, neighbors, DNS, TCP/UDP, packet capture
outcomes: Interpret route/neighbor/socket/capture evidence and trace packets across host networking layers.

nodes.title: Netfilter, nftables, connection tracking, and NAT
outcomes: Explain hook points, stateful filtering, connection tracking, NAT, and build auditable nftables policies.

nodes.title: Namespaces: isolated views of Linux resources
outcomes: Explain PID, mount, network, UTS, IPC, user, and cgroup namespaces and construct small isolation labs.

nodes.title: cgroups v2: hierarchical resource accounting and control
outcomes: Relate cgroup hierarchy/controllers to CPU, memory, I/O, process placement, and service/container resource control.

nodes.title: Linux security primitives: capabilities, ACLs, seccomp, and SELinux/LSM
outcomes: Layer discretionary access, capabilities, syscall filtering, and mandatory access control instead of reducing security to root versus non-root.

nodes.title: Containers without magic: namespaces, cgroups, mounts, and images
outcomes: Explain what a container runtime assembles from Linux primitives and identify what containers do not virtualize.

nodes.title: Observability toolkit: strace, lsof, ss, procfs, journal, vmstat, iostat
outcomes: Select tools by question, correlate multiple evidence sources, and distinguish observation from interpretation.

nodes.title: Performance measurement with perf and system counters
outcomes: Measure CPU/time/event behavior, build baselines, and avoid common benchmark and sampling misinterpretations.

nodes.title: Failure recovery: rescue environments, cores, boot failure, and storage damage
outcomes: Recover from representative service, boot, process, and filesystem failures using reversible diagnostic steps and backups.

nodes.title: Reproducible administration and configuration automation
outcomes: Turn one-off commands into documented, idempotent, reviewable system changes and distinguish imperative from declarative automation.

nodes.title: Build a Linux system from source as an integration capstone
outcomes: Use Linux From Scratch as an integration exercise to connect toolchain, libraries, filesystem hierarchy, boot, services, packages, and kernel/userspace boundaries.

nodes.title: Linux ABI, libc wrappers, and the syscall path
outcomes: Distinguish API from ABI, libc wrapper from syscall, architecture calling convention from kernel semantics, and compatibility promises from implementation details.

nodes.title: Threads, scheduling, futexes, affinity, and CPU topology
outcomes: Relate pthread-like threads to kernel tasks, futex-based synchronization, scheduling policy, CPU affinity, and observed latency.

nodes.title: Virtual-memory internals: page tables, reclaim, swap, OOM, and memory pressure
outcomes: Trace faults and reclaim at a mechanistic level and diagnose pressure using page-cache, swap, OOM, and PSI evidence.

nodes.title: Kernel memory allocation: buddy, slab/SLUB, and object lifetimes
outcomes: Explain the distinct roles of page and object allocators and connect allocator behavior to fragmentation, caches, and debugging.

nodes.title: Pathname lookup and VFS internals
outcomes: Trace a pathname through dentries/inodes/mounts/open-file state and reason about caching, lookup races, and filesystem abstraction.

nodes.title: Writeback, journaling, and filesystem implementation tradeoffs
outcomes: Relate dirty pages, writeback, ordering, journaling/checkpointing, and crash semantics to real filesystem behavior.

nodes.title: Block I/O, queues, direct I/O, asynchronous I/O, and io_uring foundations
outcomes: Trace storage requests through cache/direct paths and introduce modern asynchronous I/O and queueing tradeoffs.

nodes.title: Linux networking internals: socket to packet to device
outcomes: Trace send/receive paths through sockets, protocol layers, routing, packet buffers, qdisc, and driver boundaries.

nodes.title: Netlink and rtnetlink as kernel/userspace control planes
outcomes: Understand message-based kernel/userspace networking configuration and observe how modern iproute2-like tools communicate state.

nodes.title: eBPF architecture: programs, verifier, maps, hooks, and safety
outcomes: Explain eBPF execution/verification, maps, helper interfaces, attachment points, and why the model differs from ordinary userspace code.

nodes.title: cgroups v2 internals, pressure, and service/container integration
outcomes: Analyze hierarchical resource control, pressure signals, delegation, and interaction with systemd/container workloads.

nodes.title: Namespaces, user namespaces, mount propagation, and isolation edge cases
outcomes: Reason about namespace composition, privilege translation, mount propagation, and the limits/security implications of isolation.

nodes.title: Linux security architecture: LSM, SELinux, seccomp, capabilities, and attack surface
outcomes: Analyze layered policy enforcement and use denials/audit evidence to reason about security rather than disabling controls.

nodes.title: Kernel modules, symbols, taint, and module lifecycle
outcomes: Build/load/unload a minimal module in a safe VM and explain symbols, dependencies, taint, and why modules execute with kernel privilege.

nodes.title: Configure, build, boot, and compare Linux kernels
outcomes: Build a kernel reproducibly, manage configuration, install to a disposable VM, preserve rollback, and compare behavior across configurations.

nodes.title: ftrace, tracepoints, kprobes, and dynamic kernel tracing
outcomes: Use tracefs/ftrace/events/kprobes to test precise hypotheses about kernel execution and latency.

nodes.title: perf, PMU events, profiles, and causal performance analysis
outcomes: Design profiling experiments, interpret sampling and hardware counters cautiously, and connect hot paths to code and workload behavior.

nodes.title: eBPF tracing with bpftrace/libbpf-style workflows
outcomes: Build tracing experiments using BPF maps/events while understanding verifier, overhead, and kernel-version constraints.

nodes.title: Userspace and kernel crash debugging
outcomes: Analyze core dumps, stack traces, symbols, oops/panic evidence, and distinguish symptom from root cause.

nodes.title: Kernel diagnostics: dynamic debug, SysRq, pstore, crash evidence
outcomes: Use kernel diagnostic facilities in controlled environments and preserve evidence across failure/reboot boundaries.

nodes.title: KVM/QEMU and Linux as a virtualization host
outcomes: Explain hardware-assisted virtualization from the Linux host perspective and build an observable VM lab without confusing VMs with containers.

nodes.title: NUMA, huge pages, affinity, topology, and locality
outcomes: Measure topology/locality effects and reason about CPU/memory placement without assuming more locality is always better.

nodes.title: Design a filesystem and syscall performance experiment
outcomes: Form a falsifiable hypothesis, define workload/metrics/confounders, run repeated measurements, and interpret variance.

nodes.title: Build an isolated multi-host network laboratory with namespaces
outcomes: Construct routers/hosts/links with namespaces and virtual interfaces, observe packet paths, inject failures, and explain each layer.

nodes.title: Container runtime anatomy: rootfs, overlay, pivot_root, namespaces, cgroups
outcomes: Assemble a minimal container-like environment from Linux primitives and identify security/operational gaps a production runtime fills.

nodes.title: Navigate the kernel source tree, history, and subsystem ownership
outcomes: Map source directories to subsystems, use git history/MAINTAINERS, and follow a userspace-visible behavior into implementation.

nodes.title: Kernel concurrency: atomics, locks, memory ordering, and context constraints
outcomes: Reason about race freedom, sleepability, interrupt/process contexts, atomics/locks, and ordering rather than copying locking patterns.

nodes.title: Read-copy-update (RCU) as a concurrency design
outcomes: Explain grace periods, readers/updaters, lifetime rules, and identify when RCU changes the design space.

nodes.title: Scheduler internals and latency tradeoffs
outcomes: Trace runnable tasks through scheduling decisions and analyze fairness, latency, affinity, priority, and topology tradeoffs.

nodes.title: Memory-management internals and reclaim algorithms
outcomes: Study allocator/reclaim/page-table code paths and explain performance/failure behavior from implementation evidence.

nodes.title: Implement and reason about VFS/filesystem paths
outcomes: Read and modify a constrained filesystem/VFS path in a test kernel while preserving consistency and lifetime invariants.

nodes.title: Block/storage internals and modern I/O interfaces
outcomes: Analyze block queues, completion, direct/async I/O, device-mapper layers, and workload-dependent latency/throughput tradeoffs.

nodes.title: Networking subsystem internals and packet-processing fast paths
outcomes: Read packet-processing paths, synchronization/data structures, and compare conventional stack paths with BPF/XDP fast paths.

nodes.title: Linux driver model and a minimal device driver
outcomes: Relate buses/devices/drivers/resources/lifetimes and implement a minimal safe driver or pseudo-device in a VM.

nodes.title: Advanced eBPF/XDP program lifecycle and performance
outcomes: Analyze verifier constraints, CO-RE/libbpf-style portability, map/concurrency choices, XDP paths, and measurement overhead.

nodes.title: io_uring and asynchronous I/O design tradeoffs
outcomes: Study shared rings, submission/completion, polling/registration choices, security history, and workload-dependent benefits.

nodes.title: Kernel self-protection, exploit surface, and hardening mechanisms
outcomes: Connect memory/concurrency/ABI attack surfaces to hardening, mitigations, LSMs, sanitizers, and threat models.

nodes.title: Real-time Linux, preemption, and latency engineering
outcomes: Analyze preemption/interrupt/scheduling sources of latency and design measurements for real-time constraints.

nodes.title: Kernel testing: selftests, KUnit, sanitizers, fuzzing, and regression discipline
outcomes: Choose test layers, use kernel test/debug tooling, reproduce regressions, and design changes that remain bisectable.

nodes.title: Performance engineering across CPU, memory, I/O, and network bottlenecks
outcomes: Build a whole-system performance model and distinguish saturation, contention, latency, throughput, locality, and measurement overhead.

nodes.title: Subsystem specialization capstone
outcomes: Select one kernel subsystem, map architecture/interfaces/tests/maintainers, reproduce a nontrivial behavior, and produce a technical dossier.

nodes.title: Source and commit archaeology: reconstruct why Linux behaves this way
outcomes: Use source, git history, release/patch context, and ABI documentation to reconstruct a behavior and its design evolution.

nodes.title: Kernel development community, maintainers, patches, and review
outcomes: Identify subsystem ownership, prepare bisectable changes, select recipients, respond to review, and distinguish technical from process requirements.

nodes.title: Reproduce a bug or regression and use git bisect scientifically
outcomes: Create a minimal reproducer, control environment/version variables, bisect cause, and preserve evidence suitable for maintainers.

nodes.title: Benchmarking and experimental design for Linux systems
outcomes: Define hypotheses, baselines, controls, repetition/statistics, confounders, and measurement validity for systems experiments.

nodes.title: Read systems research papers as an engineer and reviewer
outcomes: Extract question, model, assumptions, baselines, methodology, evidence, limitations, and transferability from a systems paper.

nodes.title: Reproduce or challenge a published Linux/systems result
outcomes: Reproduce a result or failure claim, document deviations, quantify uncertainty, and separate non-reproduction from refutation.

nodes.title: Review code, patches, and performance claims
outcomes: Review correctness, concurrency, ABI, security, test coverage, performance evidence, and maintainability with explicit reasoning.

nodes.title: Research ethics, responsible disclosure, reproducibility, and community impact
outcomes: Handle vulnerabilities/bugs responsibly, preserve reproducibility, communicate limitations, and interact productively with maintainers/users.

nodes.title: Build a dated Linux research-frontier map
outcomes: Survey recent primary work and kernel development activity, identify active subareas/disagreements/open problems, and stamp the map with a refresh date.

nodes.title: Formulate a research question that survives contact with the system
outcomes: Turn an observed limitation or unexplained behavior into a falsifiable research question with measurable outcomes and credible baselines.

nodes.title: Build and evaluate a research prototype or kernel experiment
outcomes: Implement the smallest artifact that tests the hypothesis, evaluate across relevant workloads/configurations, and document threats to validity.

nodes.title: Produce a contribution-grade research report and refresh the frontier
outcomes: Write a reproducible technical report or contribution, respond to critique, and feed new evidence/questions back into the frontier map.
